OPTION A - UPSCALE A SphereSfM COLMAP DATASET (camera-sorted)

USE THIS when your SphereSfM node ran in mode=colmap_now (the default) and you
already have a cube-face COLMAP dataset (images/ + sparse/0/). It upscales that
dataset IN PLACE.

WHY camera-sorted: the cube reprojecer writes 6 faces per video frame. Read
lexically (frame-by-frame) the view direction flips 6x per frame, so a temporal
upscaler has no stable context. 'Load Dataset Images Ordered' reads the
p2s_dataset.json marker and loads each cube FACE as a coherent per-view sub-video
(camera-major), then writes every upscaled frame back to its ORIGINAL filename so
COLMAP sparse/0/images.bin still matches.

HOW TO USE
- Set 'dataset_name' on the Load node to your SphereSfM output_name.
- Keep 'lowres_suffix' identical on the Load and Save nodes.
- order_names flows Load -> Save automatically; don't edit it.

SAFE + IDEMPOTENT
- First run: images/ -> images_lowres/ (kept forever); upscaled frames written
  into images/ under the SAME filenames.
- Re-run: reads originals from images_lowres/; overwrites images/.

BATCH SIZE (important): SeedVR2 chunks frames as range(0, total, batch_size) from
frame 0, blind to the per-view boundaries. batch_size is preset to 81 so every chunk
lands inside ONE 81-frame view: no temporal bleed across seams and no ragged final
batch. The Load node also PRINTS a 'suggested_batch_size' to the console (largest 4n+1
divisor of your actual per-view length) -- if your WAN length isn't 81, set batch_size
to that printed value. OOM? drop to the next 4n+1 divisor down (81 -> 9), or lower
resolution / enable VAE tiling / DiT offload. uniform_batch_size is ON as a safety
net. Do NOT use 5/13/21 -- they don't divide 81 and will straddle seams.
